script: For 11 days from 25 August 2025, the North Sea Link, the 1.4 GW cable between Norway and Britain, carried almost nothing.
Before that it had been bringing about 1,209 MW into Britain on average. Our flow data shows when the flow stopped and restarted; it does not say why.
GB's system price averaged £72/MWh during the gap, against £84/MWh in the fortnight before. Norway's price went from €77 to €79/MWh.
Prices move for many reasons at once, so this is a before-and-after, not a measurement of the cable alone.
caveats: The cause (maintenance, fault, or a market decision) is not in our data.
Before-and-after price comparisons are not causal.
